references.text: The same principle of sharing according to the number of people in the household applies to the Passover lamb—each person should have enough according to their need.
Fulfillment of the command: when they measured it, the one who gathered much had nothing left over, and the one who gathered little had no lack.
Explanation of the unit of measure omer—one omer is a tenth of an ephah.
The expression 'לגלגלת' (per head) is also used in the census of Israel.
The same principle of distribution according to the number of people: inheritances were to be allocated based on the size of the tribes.
A similar principle of fair distribution: the spoils were divided equally between those who fought and those who stayed with the equipment.
Paul quotes this principle regarding the omer and fair distribution in connection with the collection for the poor in Jerusalem.
Direct narrative continuation; 16:32 establishes the preservation order for the manna gathered according to the instruction in 16:16.
Thematic parallel concerning God's supernatural provision and abundance in the wilderness versus a prophetic miracle.
Complementary instructions within the same event; 16:23 expands on the 'need' principle from 16:16 by including Sabbath preparation.
Thematic parallel concerning divine instruction about food supply and preparation in an emergency situation (the flood versus the wilderness journey).
